## High Level Overview of Change

This PR:
* Makes `addSLE` in `DIDSet` a static function, instead of a free function.
* Renames `Attestation` to `Data` everywhere (an artifact of a previous name for the field).
* Actually runs a set of tests that were not included in the `run` function of `DID_test`.

### Context of Change

AI code review

> **Description:**
> The helper function `addSLE` is a free function defined in the `xrpl` namespace with external linkage, no declaration in any header, and no `static` keyword:
> 
> ```cpp
> TER
> addSLE(ApplyContext& ctx, std::shared_ptr<SLE> const& sle, AccountID const& owner)
> ```
> 
> This function is logically private to `DIDSet.cpp`. As written:
> 1. It pollutes the `xrpl` namespace and could conflict with similarly named functions in other TUs.
> 2. It creates a potential ODR (One Definition Rule) violation risk.
> 3. It can be accidentally called from other translation units that include the right headers.
> 
> The fix is to declare it `static` or move it into an anonymous namespace (as is done consistently throughout the rest of the codebase — see `DeleteAccount.cpp` which uses `namespace { ... }` for all its helpers).

### API Impact

N/A

Suggested commit message:
```
`DID`: Decentralized identifiers (DIDs) (XLS-40): (#4636)

Implement native support for W3C DIDs.

Add a new ledger object: `DID`.

Add two new transactions:
1. `DIDSet`: create or update the `DID` object.
2. `DIDDelete`: delete the `DID` object.

This meets the requirements specified in the DID v1.0 specification
currently recommended by the W3C Credentials Community Group.

The DID format for the XRP Ledger conforms to W3C DID standards. The
objects can be created and owned by any XRPL account holder. The
transactions can be integrated by any service, wallet, or application.
```

reviews.author: nbougalis
reviews.body: Left some comments. Biggest issue, IMO, is the lack of any invariant checks. You should consider what types of checks make sense to code up.

reviews.author: seelabs
reviews.body: Looks good. Left some minor comments.

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body: Shouldn't there be _some_ sanity checks for these values? At a minimum, a length check, so that someone can't create a megabyte or two worth of data?

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body:
You _should_ be able to just reduce this `if`/`else` with:

```
(*sleDID)[~sfURI] = ctx_.tx[~sfURI];
```

Notice that you don't check if one or both the URI and DATA fields are being set to the same value that they already hold; so it's possible for someone to "update" the object while making no change. You may want to elide the call to `update` in that case.

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body:
This can be reduced to just `return addSLE(ctx_, sleDID, account_);`

Also, why even have `addSLE` as a separate function instead of inlining the code here?

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body: No need for the separate variable of the block scope.

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body: Same comment as before: why a separate function instead of inlining the code?

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body: This bit could be done in `preclaim`; not sure it makes sense to do it, just pointing it out.

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body:
This conflicts with PR #4626: see [lines 302-305 of TER.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/pull/4626/files#diff-570760ccc79d416a7e98bf3e851c2e298ea5cf90f7207018e06aa6b46d09a013R302-R305):

```
    tecAMM_EMPTY = 166,
    tecAMM_NOT_EMPTY = 167,
    tecAMM_ACCOUNT = 168,
    tecINCOMPLETE = 169
```

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body: You may want to consider using a non-common code here? On the other hand `Data` is generic enough that it may be useful elsewhere, so... maybe it's fine.

reviewCommentsList.author: mvadari
reviewCommentsList.body: It seems overly complicated to add that to `preclaim`.

reviewCommentsList.author: cjcobb23
reviewCommentsList.body: I feel like `DID` is a weird name for this object. This is just a ledger object that holds two arbitrary bits of data, in the `URI` field and the `Data` field. Why not call this something more generic? I could see this being used for things other than DID.

reviewCommentsList.author: cjcobb23
reviewCommentsList.body: Similar to my other comment, why not call these something more generic instead of `DIDSet` and `DIDDelete`?

reviewCommentsList.author: mvadari
reviewCommentsList.body: You can only own one of them, so I don't really know what else you'd use them for.

reviewCommentsList.author: mvadari
reviewCommentsList.body:
I don't think that reduction works.
What I want is: do nothing if the field doesn't exist in the transaction, delete the field if the field is an empty string, and replace it in any other case. 
What my understanding of that line of code is: delete the field if it doesn't exist, and replace it in any other case.

reviewCommentsList.author: cjcobb23
reviewCommentsList.body: This is just arbitrary data storage, I could really use this for anything at all. I could use it for an oracle, a bridge, governance, etc.

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body: You're right, given what you're trying to do my proposed construct won't work. It's fine as it, but I wouldn't have personally structured this as you have; I'd have included two flags that, if set, indicate the type of value you're setting/clearing. So, if `sfFlags & flagURI` was set, then the `URI` field is replaced with the `URI` field from the transaction.

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body: Agreed. And any performance gains are likely to be overshadowed by the extra work to load/manipulate the objects.

reviewCommentsList.author: mvadari
reviewCommentsList.body: This was the method that @seelabs and @aanchal4 thought was most user-intuitive.

reviewCommentsList.author: seelabs
reviewCommentsList.body:
That's an interesting point @cjcobb23 

We could make this more generic - add a read-only "kind" field that's part of the hash and let people store whatever data they want.

So a DID would be stored in this new generic data object and have a "kind" of "DID", oracles would have a "kind" of "oracle-usd-xrp" or somesuch, and since the "kind" is part of the hash they are distinct objects. Although with this design you can only ever have one object per "kind", but that doesn't seem too bad.

We have talked about general purpose data storage in the past, now that we have a concrete use-case for such an object (DIDs) it seems like it's worth looking at doing the generic solution. We'd have to flesh it out a little more if we want to go in this direction, but it seems like a good idea.

I'd probably rename the fields, maybe add a couple more fields, and a read-only "kind" and everything else works as-is now. It's an easy change from an implementation POV.

One problem with the generic solution is getting everyone to agree on what "kind" means. I might want ids to be "IDS", you might want "DID", and someone else whatever the french word for "ID" is. But that doesn't seem like a killer.

One thing I think worth thinking about is actually storing the schema in the object. The schema could be defined in protobuf. reviewCommentsList.author: mDuo13
reviewCommentsList.body:
I think we should rename the ledger entry `Document` ("DID documents" are a thing but this can store any type of document), change the transaction names to `DocumentSet` and `DocumentDelete`, and allow multiple such items per account, with each having a (required) UInt32 `DocumentNumber` field to uniquely identify the doc. Conventionally, certain numbers can be reserved for certain types of documents—like 0 could be for a decentralized ID. That's similar to the "kind" that @seelabs suggested, but it takes up less space and we'd have to worry less about normalizing i.e. capitalization. You still need to know various outside conventions to use the "kind" identifier anyway so numbers are about as useful as text in that regard.

I care about size because this object is already pushing up against the limits of how large a single user-facing ledger object can safely be. Excessive trust line creation caused problems not _that_ long ago and they're max 380 bytes—this one can up to 564 by my count. So, probably best not to store a user-facing description field on-chain too.

Users could add additional metadata or more info to their `xrp-ledger.toml` file (or DNS TXT records, like NFTs, I suppose) if they want to provide contextual info about the documents they're storing in the ledger. Or, alternatively, they could put it in transaction memos and users could look those up if they really needed to.

I think this sort of "general document storage" functionality can find many use cases, including DID, oracles, and more like tracking the history or provenance of specific items. The difference from NFTs is that these documents are meant to be mutable (by owner), and not bought, sold, or traded like NFTs are.

issues.title: Incomplete preflight `temEMPTY_DID` check in DIDSet allows subset-empty transactions to bypass preflight
issues.author: mvadari
issues.body:
## Issue Description

The second preflight guard in `DIDSet::preflight()` (`src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/did/DIDSet.cpp:32–35`) requires **all three** fields (`sfURI`, `sfDIDDocument`, `sfData`) to be simultaneously present AND empty to return `temEMPTY_DID`:

```cpp
if (ctx.tx.isFieldPresent(sfURI) && ctx.tx[sfURI].empty() &&
    ctx.tx.isFieldPresent(sfDIDDocument) && ctx.tx[sfDIDDocument].empty() &&
    ctx.tx.isFieldPresent(sfData) && ctx.tx[sfData].empty())
    return temEMPTY_DID;
```

This misses cases where only a **subset** of fields are present and all of them are empty. For example, a transaction containing only `{sfURI="", sfDIDDocument=""}` (without `sfData`) passes preflight because `isFieldPresent(sfData)` is false, breaking the AND chain.

The logical intent should be: "if every field that IS present is empty, and at least one field is present, reject at preflight."

With `fixEmptyDID` enabled, these subset-empty transactions are caught at `doApply` time with `tecEMPTY_DID` (fee charged), rather than at preflight with `temEMPTY_DID` (no fee charged). Ideally, these should be caught at preflight to save unnecessary compute across the network.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Submit a `DIDSet` transaction with only a subset of fields present and all empty, e.g. `{sfURI="", sfDIDDocument=""}` (no `sfData`).
2. Observe that the transaction passes preflight (the `temEMPTY_DID` check on lines 32–35 is not triggered).
3. With `fixEmptyDID` enabled, the transaction fails at `doApply` with `tecEMPTY_DID` (fee is charged).

## Expected Result

The preflight check should catch **all** subset-empty cases and return `temEMPTY_DID` (no fee charged), preventing the transaction from being broadcast across the network unnecessarily.

For example, the check could be restructured to: "if at least one field is present, and every present field is empty, return `temEMPTY_DID`."

## Actual Result

Only the case where **all three** fields are present and empty is caught at preflight. Subset cases (e.g. only `sfURI=""` or `sfURI="" + sfDIDDocument=""`) bypass preflight and are only caught at `doApply` time with `tecEMPTY_DID`, resulting in:
- The transaction fee being charged to the sender.
- Unnecessary compute spent across the network (preclaim + doApply execution).

## Environment

- **Source:** `develop` branch, commit `12954d5392294338081ba941012e9b5055a5cbaa`
- **File:** `src/libxrpl/tx/transactors/did/DIDSet.cpp`, lines 32–35 (preflight) and lines 128–132 (doApply `fixEmptyDID` guard)

issues.title: My rippled API missed a transaction, and maybe wisepass.com's did too
issues.author: miracle2k
issues.body:
Namely this one:

https://wisepass.com/tx/9A54E63E14CFF3FD5797E4950DF212966B89949BCDF26DCE3F94B99082D72376

The transaction is stated as being included in ledger 4279703.

When I queried that ledger using `{"command": "ledger", "transactions" : true, "ledger_index": 4279703, "expand": true}` the response was marked as closed and contained no transaction (I don't have the actual output anymore).

The funny thing is that the ledger is also empty on the wisepass site:

https://wisepass.com/ledger/4279703

I am guessing they might be subscribing to the ledger feed and the transaction feed separately.

Subsequently my ledger-subscription claimed that 4279704 was closed, and as described in #248, querying _that_ id gave me a "closed: False" response that included the transaction in question, officially committed to 4279703.

Am I doing something wrong in general that I am running into these?
